overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair had discretion to let a member speak during public comment, and the unnoticed topic was not shown to be reasonably anticipated by the chair.

allegations.summary: A committee member raised, during public comment, a matter not listed on the January 6 meeting notice, allegedly to avoid placing it on the agenda.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that neither the Committee nor Mr. Tinkham violated the Open Meeting Law when Mr. Tinkham made his comment during the January 6 meeting.

allegations.summary: A complaint alleged a committee member misused the public comment portion of the meeting by commenting as a member rather than as a member of the public.
allegations.key_passage: the fact that Mr. Tinkham made a comment during this portion of the meeting, in and of itself, does not violate the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
